styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Kapaleeshwarar temple, San Thome and the Mylapore lanes.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Filter coffee, dosas and Chettinad heat.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Marina sands, Elliot's Beach and sunset walks.

stays.why: Old-quarter lanes, the big temple and San Thome basilica on foot; good for culture and food walks.
Central and well connected: Egmore station, the museum and easy buses to most sights.
Shopping heart: silk sarees, jewellery and street markets; busy and loud but handy.
Main artery with business hotels and metro stops; a short ride to Marina Beach and the fort area.

food: Start with a South Indian breakfast: idli, vada and dosa with sambar and coconut chutney. Cheap and everywhere.
Drink filter coffee in a small café or from a street stall. Order it 'strong' if you like it punchy.
Try Chettinad dishes (peppery chicken or mutton) for a hotter, deeper flavour than most Indian food you know.
Seafood is good near the coast; ask what is fresh that day and agree the price before ordering.
Vegetarian thali on a banana leaf at lunch is great value. Eat with your right hand; many places are pure veg.
more_time: Add a half-day south to Mahabalipuram for the shore temple and rock carvings; check bus or taxi times on the day.
Swap one city afternoon for the Theosophical Society gardens and Elliot's Beach in Besant Nagar.
History fans can add Fort St George and the museum inside; check opening days before you go.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the temples, the fort area and a proper food crawl; add a third for a Mahabalipuram day.

month_notes: January: mild and dry, highs near 28°C. The best month for walking the old quarters.
February: warm and almost rain-free, around 30°C. Great for beaches and sightseeing.
March: heating up to 32°C with little rain. Start early, rest at midday.
April: hot at 34°C and humid. Keep afternoons indoors or in the shade.
May: peak heat near 35°C. Do sights at sunrise and after 5pm.
June: still 35°C but rain days jump to about 12. Carry a light rain jacket.
July: wetter, around 17 rain days. Showers are often short; plan flexible days.
August: about 19 rain days and 33°C. Expect grey spells and sudden downpours.
September: one of the wettest months, about 20 rain days. Pack an umbrella.
October: still wet, around 20 rain days, highs near 31°C. Check forecasts before beach plans.
November: wettest month, about 21 rain days. The northeast monsoon can bring heavy rain and flooding; check on the day.
December: rain eases to about 12 days and it cools to 28°C. Pleasant again by late month.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, with a wet northeast-monsoon season from roughly October to December.

items.title: Best time: December to February
items.text: Highs around 28–30°C and few rain days. Ideal for temples, markets and the beach.

items.title: Hot season April to June
items.text: Highs of 34–35°C with high humidity. Sightsee early morning and evening; stay in shade at midday.

items.title: Monsoon October to December
items.text: Up to about 20 rain days a month. Rain can be heavy and cause local flooding; keep plans flexible.

items.title: Carry an umbrella May to December
items.text: Rain days rise from about 6 in May to a peak near 21 in November. Short, sharp showers are common.

items.title: Humid near the coast
items.text: Sea breezes help at Marina and Elliot's Beach, but it stays muggy most of the year. Drink water often.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, a hat and sunscreen; a light rain jacket or umbrella; modest clothing for temples (shoulders and knees covered).

transit.best: Metro for the airport and main stations; Ola or Uber for everything else.

modes.text: Blue and Green lines link the airport, Alandur and MGR Chennai Central. Fares ₹10–60. A one-day Tourist Travel Card costs ₹100, with ₹50 refunded on return.
MTC city buses are very cheap, roughly ₹4–30; deluxe and AC buses cost more. Daily and weekly passes cost about ₹50 and ₹300 on normal and deluxe routes.
Ola and Uber work well and are usually cheaper than prepaid taxis. Autos use meters or you negotiate the fare first.
Suburban trains are fast and cheap, from ₹5. Buy first class at peak times.
Not a common choice for visitors; traffic is heavy. Use apps and the metro instead.
Good in Mylapore lanes and around markets in the cooler months. Hot and humid most of the year; take shade and water.
